$comment: Hands tools served by nest-mcp as mcp__nest__<name>. Inputs are forwarded verbatim as HandsRequest.op (plus "tool": <name>). Spec: docs/interfaces/host-guest/.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command in the sandbox and returns its combined stdout/stderr.

- Each command runs in a new process. The working directory carries over between calls (a `cd` persists); exported environment variables do not.
- Quote paths that contain spaces. Prefer absolute paths.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000 (2 minutes), maximum 600000 (10 minutes). A foreground command that reaches its timeout is moved to the background instead of being killed (unless it starts with `sleep`); the result gives its task ID and output file.
- Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running processes such as dev servers or watch builds. The result returns immediately with a task ID and the path of an output file; read it with Read or poll with TaskOutput, and stop it with TaskStop. Background commands run for at most `timeout` ms (default 30 minutes, maximum 2 hours).
- Output longer than ~30000 characters is saved to a file in the sandbox; the result contains the file path and a preview of the first 2000 characters. Failed commands show a head-and-tail excerpt instead.
- Use Read, Edit, Write, Glob and Grep instead of cat/sed/echo/find/grep where they fit.
- Network access goes through the sandbox's egress policy; a request denied by policy fails with HTTP 403 and an explanation.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (foreground max 600000; background max 7200000)

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in 5-10 words, in active voice

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. Use TaskOutput or Read on the output file to read the output later.

tools.name: TaskOutput
tools.description: Retrieves output and status of a background task started with Bash `run_in_background` (or moved to the background at its timeout). Returns the task status, exit code if finished, and the most recent output (the full output is in the task's output file; Read it for everything). Set `block: true` to wait up to `timeout` ms for the task to finish.

task_id.description: The ID of the background task

block.description: Wait for the task to finish before returning

timeout.description: Maximum time to wait in milliseconds when block is true (default 30000, max 600000)

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description: Stops a running background task by ID. Its process tree is killed; the output file is kept.

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the sandbox filesystem.

- `file_path` must be absolute.
- By default reads up to 2000 lines from the start of the file. Use `offset` (1-based line number) and `limit` to read a range; read large files in pages.
- Output uses `cat -n` format: line number, a tab, then the line. Lines longer than 2000 characters are truncated.
- A whole-file read over 256 KB, or a range over the output limit, returns an error asking for a smaller range or a Grep search.
- Images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) are returned as images you can see. PDFs: pass `pages` (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages) for documents over 10 pages. Jupyter notebooks return all cells with outputs.
- Reads only files, not directories; list directories with `ls` via Bash.
- Reading a file is required before editing or overwriting it with Edit or Write.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from

limit.description: The number of lines to read

pages.description: Page range for PDF files, e.g. "1-5" (max 20 pages per request)

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the sandbox filesystem, creating parent directories as needed and overwriting any existing file.

- `file_path` must be absolute.
- An existing file must have been read with Read first in this session; otherwise the write fails.
- Prefer Edit for partial changes to existing files.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file before editing it.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including whitespace and indentation (do not include the line-number prefix from Read output).
- The edit fails if `old_string` is not found, or appears more than once and `replace_all` is false; add surrounding context to make it unique, or set `replace_all` to replace every occurrence.
- If the file changed on disk since you read it, the edit still applies when `old_string` matches the current content exactly once; the result says so, and you should re-read before edits that depend on surrounding content.
- Only valid UTF-8 (or UTF-16LE with BOM) files can be edited.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description:
Fast file pattern matching in the sandbox.

- Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts".
- Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time (newest first), at most 100; a truncation note appears when the cap is hit.
- Does not respect .gitignore.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. Defaults to the current working directory.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
A search tool built on ripgrep, run in the sandbox.

- Full regex syntax (ripgrep, not POSIX grep): literal braces need escaping, e.g. `interface\{\}`.
- Filter files with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "files_with_matches" (default, paths only), "content" (matching lines; supports -n, -A, -B, -C), "count" (matches per file plus a total).
- Patterns match within single lines unless `multiline` is true.
- Respects .gitignore; pass a path directly to search an ignored file.
- `head_limit` limits entries returned (default 250); `offset` skips entries for paging.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in. Defaults to the current working directory.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type), e.g. js, py, rust, go

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (content mode)

-A.description: Lines to show after each match (content mode)

-B.description: Lines to show before each match (content mode)

-C.description: Lines to show before and after each match (content mode)

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines

head_limit.description: Limit output to the first N entries (default 250)

offset.description: Skip the first N entries before applying head_limit
